title: Except the fear of heaven (Berakhot 33b)
hook: everything is in heaven's hands except the fear of heaven
tomorrow: a long prayer or a short one: which does a scared family need?

segments.voice: Yesterday, keep praying: Chanina ben Dosa didn't stop for a snake at his heel, and the sages still said stop for a scorpion. Today, the one thing that's in your hands.

The night before surgery, the family gets a call: be there by six, nothing to eat after midnight, the doctor will explain the risks. Every line of it is about things no one in the family controls. The Talmud has a sentence for that list. Rabbi Chanina says: everything is in the hands of heaven, except the fear of heaven. Then it proves it with a verse, and the verse makes the whole thing sound small. That's the puzzle.
screen: `BE THERE BY SIX.` → `ALL IN HEAVEN'S HANDS.` → `EXCEPT ONE THING.`

segments.voice: Here's the verse, Moses speaking in Deuteronomy: "what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God." Only that? As if awe were a light errand. The Talmud notices, and asks it straight: is the fear of heaven a small thing? Its answer is honest. Yes, for Moses it was small. Then a parable. Someone asked for a big vessel he already owns: it feels small to him. Asked for a small one he doesn't own, it feels huge. Moses had awe, so asking for it sounded easy. For the rest of us it's the big vessel we haven't got yet. Fear of heaven, yirat shamayim, here sits closer to awe than to terror: living as if God is really there. And notice what the line hands you. The weather, the diagnosis, the surgeon's steady hands: heaven's. How you stand inside all that, whether you meet it with reverence or let it go flat, Rabbi Chanina leaves with you. The one thing that's yours is not small. It's the hardest thing on the list, and it can't be done for you.
screen: `ONLY TO FEAR? SO SMALL?` · `SMALL, FOR MOSES.` · `THE VESSEL YOU DON'T OWN.` · `THE ONE THING LEFT WITH YOU.` · then, large: `AWE IS YOURS TO CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Pick up one ordinary object near you: a cup, a leaf, your own hand. Look at it for the whole sit as if you had never seen one before. That attention is the part no one can choose for you.
screen: `ONE ORDINARY OBJECT.` · `AS IF FOR THE FIRST TIME.` · `YOUR CHOICE.`

segments.voice: Except the fear of heaven. Everything is in heaven's hands but your own awe, which the Talmud says only felt small to Moses.
screen: `EXCEPT THE FEAR OF HEAVEN — today's word`.

segments.voice: Keep this one close: awe is yours to choose, even when nothing else is. Twenty-seven of fifty.

screen: `DAY 1514 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 27 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: A LONG PRAYER OR A SHORT ONE?`

howItsDone: Yirat shamayim, fear or awe of heaven, is a phrase Jews use for a person's reverence for God; Rabbi Chanina's line, 'everything is in the hands of heaven except the fear of heaven,' is often quoted when people talk about free choice.

fork.setup: your team loses the final on a bad call. on the bus home, everyone is either raging at the ref or scrolling in silence. what does Rabbi Chanina's line leave in your hands?
options: nothing: the call was out of your control, so how you react is too.

fork.reveal: everything is in the hands of heaven except the fear of heaven. the call isn't yours; the way you stand inside it is.

original.note: Hebrew: fear (awe) of heaven; 'heaven' here is a way of saying God.

trapdoor: what you thought: be scared of God, because everything is decided anyway.
what it means: nearly everything is out of your hands; your own reverence isn't, and it isn't small.
what a scholar hears: Berakhot 33b reads Deuteronomy 10:12's 'but to fear' as asking little, then answers: little for Moses, with the parable of the large and small vessels.
guess: your own awe is the one thing heaven leaves you to choose

a blessing said when you look up at the open sky

chat.says: surgery's at 7am tmrw. surgeon decides, anesthesia decides. what do i even get to choose here
options: How you show up: your own awe and care. The Talmud says that part stays yours.

Push the doctors hard enough and the outcome is partly yours to choose.
chat.meaning: Everything is in heaven's hands except the fear of heaven: how you meet what happens, with reverence, is the one thing left with you.

yirat shamayim.meaning: fear or awe of heaven: reverence for God

Rabbi Chanina.meaning: the sage who says everything but awe is in heaven's hands

Deuteronomy.meaning: the fifth book of the Torah, Moses' last speeches

Talmud.meaning: the sages' long discussion of Jewish law and story
